turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody picked up the phone to call me first. I have a call at 4:40, so start with who decided that, and when.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"That's the end of it." Your own school's procedure, 4.3, says software alone does not establish a concern, and the company that sells it says not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student; I have that printed in my bag. So either you have something else, Hale, or I'm walking upstairs to the principal at 4:30.
I don't need more proof than that.

"I don't need more proof than that." I'm writing that down, word for word, along with the time you said it. One more question before I go upstairs, Hale: did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in, yes or no?
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.

"Unlike some people." My child never lies, Hale, so say his name if that's what you mean, or are you calling me a liar as well? Either way, that sentence is going in my complaint to the principal tonight, and you still haven't told me whether anyone heard Owen before you entered that mark.

Then we're done here, and I'm going straight to the principal's office to ask for a review under 4.6 of your own procedure. If that doesn't fix it, it goes to the board under section 42 of the Education Act, and I'll want everything you entered on Owen's file in writing by tomorrow, Wednesday. Last chance, Hale: is there a single document with a date on it, or not?
